sounds.name: Filter Sweep
sounds.ref: The manual’s classic filter sweep: a closed, fully resonant filter opened slowly by the envelope
sounds.blurb: Long notes that swell in and open from a dark rumble into a whistling, resonant sweep.
sounds.how: The filter starts closed with Resonance at full, so on its own it lets almost nothing through. The envelope does two jobs: with Amp Mod lit it fades each note in over Attack, and through Filter Amt it opens the cutoff at the same time, so the resonance rides up through the harmonics as the note swells. The settings are the manual’s, its times found on this app’s knobs.

steps.title: Close the filter and turn the resonance up
steps.why:
With the cutoff at the bottom the saw is shut out, and full Resonance leaves a quiet ring at the cutoff.
- Cutoff 0 · 30 Hz
- Resonance 100
- Listen for: almost nothing: a faint, low rumble.

steps.title: Let the envelope shape the loudness
steps.why:
Amp Mod hands the amplifier to the envelope: a slow Attack fades each note in, a long Decay/Rel lets it fade out after you let go, and Sustain holds it near the top.
- Amp Mod lit
- Attack 81 · 1.7 s
- Decay / Rel 94 · 7.9 s
- Sustain 90
- Listen for: still dark, but now each note fades in.

steps.title: Open the filter with the envelope
steps.why:
Filter Amt sends the same envelope to the cutoff, so the filter opens as the note swells.
- Filter Amt 70
- Listen for: each note rising out of the dark with a whistling sweep, then closing slowly after you let go.

sounds.name: Sci-Fi Computer
sounds.ref: The manual’s random bleeps: the LFO’s random steps sent to the pitch, the computer of an old science-fiction film
sounds.blurb: A held note that jumps to a new random pitch four times a second, like a film computer thinking.
sounds.how: The LFO’s Random shape holds a new random value for each of its cycles, a sample and hold. The matrix point where the LFO row meets Pitch sends it to the oscillator, so every cycle lands the note on a new pitch. The manual gives the LFO at about 4 Hz and the point at about 30.

- LFO shape Random
- Rate 57 · 4.12 Hz
- Listen for: nothing yet: the LFO reaches the sound only through the matrix.

steps.title: Send it to the pitch
steps.why:
The point at LFO and Pitch sets how far the LFO moves the pitch.
- LFO > Pitch 30
- Listen for: the note jumping to a new pitch four times a second.

sounds.name: Pitch Blip
sounds.ref: The manual’s first cycling envelope patch: a quick rise in pitch at the start of each note
sounds.blurb: Short notes that each scoop up in pitch and drop back, a playful video-game blip.
sounds.how: The cycling envelope rises once on each note in Env mode. With no hold and no fall it climbs over Rise and drops straight back, and the matrix point at CycEnv and Pitch sends that climb to the oscillator, scaled by Amount. The manual gives the point, the times and the amount; the short envelope on the loudness is this lesson’s, to make each note a blip.

steps.title: A quick rise and no fall
steps.why:
In Env mode the cycling envelope runs once per note: Rise sets how long it climbs, and with Hold/Sustain and Fall at 0 it drops straight back. Amount sets how much of it the matrix gets.
- Rise 58 · 210 ms
- Hold / Sustain 0 · sustain 0
- Fall 0 · 1 ms
- Amount 50
- Listen for: nothing yet: the cycling envelope is not sent anywhere.

steps.title: Send it to the pitch
steps.why:
The point at CycEnv and Pitch makes each note scoop upwards.
- CycEnv > Pitch 20
- Listen for: each note sliding up a couple of semitones as it starts.

steps.title: Make each note a blip
steps.why:
Amp Mod lets the envelope shape the loudness: no sustain and a short decay make a short note.
- Amp Mod lit
- Decay / Rel 40 · 85 ms
- Sustain 0
- Listen for: short, bouncing blips that chirp upwards.

sounds.blurb: Short, punchy minor-seventh chords, each played with a single finger.
sounds.how: The Chords model plays four oscillators at a chord’s notes over the key you press, so one finger plays the whole chord; Wave picks the chord. Paraphony is off in Chords, as on the hardware, and the chord moves with each key. A short envelope on the loudness and the filter makes each chord a stab.

sounds.name: Talking Vowels

sounds.blurb: A buzzing voice that sings “a, e, i, o, u” as the notes hold.
sounds.how: The Speech model runs a buzz through three vowel formants. Its Shape picks the vowel, and the matrix has no fixed column for Shape, so an Assign column is set to it and the LFO’s point in that column sweeps it slowly. The hardware’s Speech also speaks whole words from its libraries; here it sings the vowels.

The cycling envelope in Loop mode rises and falls over a few seconds and, through its point in the Timbre column, moves that place, so the tone keeps drifting. Paraphonic plays the chord; Shape adds a chorus.

sounds.name: FM Bass
sounds.ref: A punchy two-operator FM bass whose brightness falls away on each note
sounds.blurb: A tight, rubbery bass that starts with a metallic snap and settles to a round tone.
sounds.how: Two Op.FM is a sine whose phase another sine moves: Wave sets their ratio, Timbre how hard the second moves the first (the brightness) and Shape its feedback. The envelope’s point in the Timbre column raises that amount at the start of each note and lets it fall back, as an FM synth’s modulator envelope does.
